instruction.text: Match the main and subordinate clauses together to create a sentence.

trainers.hint: A subordinate clause always needs a main clause with it to make sense. It can be at the beginning or end of the sentence.

atoms.b: I had a best friend named Jamie.

atoms.a: My family recently adopted a dog named Rover
atoms.b: after we met him at the shelter.

instruction.text: Match the main and subordinate clauses together to create a sentence.

trainers.hint: A subordinate clause always needs a main clause with it to make sense. It can be at the beginning or end of the sentence.

atoms.b: although she didn’t visit the Eiffel Tower.
because it is a nice way to see the country.

atoms.a: I had a study session with my friend Matt
atoms.b: because we had a test the next day.

instruction.text: Choose the correct subordinate clause to complete the sentence.

atoms.b: ((++Although_he_is_allergic Despite_the_fact_it_is_dark_outside)), Jamie has got a new kitten.
Gemma wants to go to the supermarket ((++even_though_it_is_miles_away because_they_sent_it_in_the_post)).
((++Even_though_it_is_expensive Since_I_was_three)), I want to go on holiday to the Maldives.
I worked really hard in school ((++because_I_wanted_good_grades once_I_was_finished)).
Phoebe will buy that t-shirt ((++once_she_has_her_monthly_pocket_money before_it_was_dark)).
((++Despite_the_fact_it_was_snowing Since_we_were_kids)), Leo and Willow went for a run in the park.
